title: Synthetic slice reconciliation and rollback mediation across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Chen
description: After a cross-environment canary deploy (hosted -> dedicated -> private) we observed customer-facing regressions for a subset of tenants. Root cause appears to be stale KV-cache / prefix-caching divergence combined with heterogeneous model variant fallbacks. This ticket coordinates a short-term rollback-mechanism, a synthetic-slice reconciliation tool to validate KV cache consistency per-tenant, and postmortem actions to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Several enterprise customers reported hallucination regressions after a canary rollout. Error surface: 2.6x spike in generation anomalies (nonsensical tokens) for 4% of requests; affected only tenants on Dedicated pools with private fallbacks. SLA breach risk for top-tier accounts; support escalations opened by Account team.
reproduction_steps: 1) Trigger canary rollout of model v2.3 to a small tenant slice in hosted region-us-west1
2) Route duplicate traffic from tenant to Dedicated pool with fallback configured to local quantized variant
3) Replay failing prompt set (shared in 'repro-prompts.csv' on Drive) at 10qps for 30 minutes
4) Observe KV cache mismatch errors in runtime logs (trace IDs noted below) and generation mismatch in evaluation harness

mitigations: A: Immediate staged rollback of v2.3 to v2.2 for affected tenant slices (hosted + dedicated) — executed 2026-03-11 02:10 UTC
B: Enable forced KVCACHE invalidation for Dedicated backend for tenant-slice-1734 (workaround flag set) — executed 2026-03-11 02:25 UTC
C: Short-term rate-limit on background replays to avoid rehydration storms — config updated in runtime-config: replay.max_qps=2
D: Customer comms: sent initial incident notice and hotfix ETA via Account team (Slack thread #acct-cust-9931)
E: Canary paused globally while triage continues

investigation_notes: KV cache divergence occurs when prefix hashing differs between quantized fallback variant and primary model; mismatch surfaced when fallback was auto-selected under memory pressure
Cross-env routing exposed a race where hosted ingress acknowledged completion before dedicated pool finished KV warmup
Telemetry gap: we lacked tenant-scoped kvcache-check metrics — added metric 'runtime.kvcache.consistency.tenant' to staging
Edge-case: tokenizer normalization mismatch between model v2.2 and local-quantized v2.2-q8 caused tokenization sharding leading to different continuation states
decisions: Short-term: keep rollback as primary mitigation for any tenant slice showing >1% generation-anomaly after rollback verification
Medium-term: build SSR (synthetic slice reconciler) to compare per-tenant KV prefix hashes pre/post rollout and reject canary if mismatch > 0
Long-term: add tokenization contract tests between model variants and quantized fallbacks during model onboarding
Operational: require dedicated warmup handshake ack (kvcache.ready) before traffic split for cross-env rollouts
